heading.en: Gold, resin and a broken mummy

hook.en: In 1922 an archaeologist opened a tomb filled with gold. But the greatest treasure, the king himself, was stuck fast to his coffin.

objectives.en: Describe Carter's discovery and the tomb's treasures
Explain why the mummy was stuck to the coffin
Evaluate how Carter handled the mummy

narration.en: In 1922 an archaeologist opened a tomb filled with gold. But the greatest treasure, the king himself, was stuck fast to his coffin.

body.en: In 1922 the British archaeologist Howard Carter discovered Tut's tomb in the Valley of the Kings. Its treasures astonished the world: gilded chariots, jewellery, statues, board games, weapons, linen clothes, and food and wine for the afterlife. The king lay inside nested coffins, the innermost made of solid gold.

narration.en: In 1922 the British archaeologist Howard Carter discovered Tut's tomb in the Valley of the Kings. Its treasures astonished the world: gilded chariots, jewellery, statues, board games, weapons, linen clothes, and food and wine for the afterlife. The king lay inside nested coffins, the innermost made of solid gold.

say.en: In 1922 Howard Carter finds the tomb.

text.en: Howard Carter, Valley of the Kings

say.en: His team records the dazzling treasures.
They find the mummy glued to the coffin by resins.
They cut it free and later reassemble it on sand.

text.en: cut at joints, laid on sand

body.en: Carter's team found that the ritual resins poured over the body had hardened like cement, gluing the mummy to the bottom of its coffin. Leaving it out in the hot sun did not loosen it. So they cut the mummy free: they removed the head and cut the body apart at the major joints, using heated knives to separate it from the gold. Carter argued that it had to be done, as robbers would otherwise have torn the body apart for its gold. The remains were later put together again on a tray of sand and returned to the tomb.

points.en: Hardened resins glued the mummy to the coffin
Head and limbs cut free with heated knives
Reassembled and returned to the tomb

problem.en: Why did Carter's team cut Tut's mummy apart?

steps.en: Ritual resins had hardened and glued the mummy to its coffin.
Placing it in the hot sun did not loosen it.
They believed robbers would destroy it for its gold anyway.

answer.en: The resins poured over the body had set like cement, fixing the mummy to the bottom of the gold coffin. When sunlight failed to loosen it, Carter's men cut the body free at the joints, believing it was the only way to remove and protect it.
